reconcile.connective: Commentators read the two events as one continuous calling: the cloak cast at Elisha's call was a provisional sign Elijah kept, and it fell to Elisha only at the ascension.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells, in The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, presses the timing as a contradiction: 1 Kings 19:19 has Elijah cast the mantle on Elisha at their first meeting, yet 2 Kings 2:13 has Elisha receive it only after Elijah is taken up.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (skepticsannotatedbible.com), "Did Elisha receive Elijah's mantle before or after Elijah is taken up into heaven?"

excerpts.excerpt_text: Elijah did but cast his mantle upon him. (Kg1 19:19) … but, when Elijah went to heaven, he had the mantle entire, Kg2 2:13.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly dissolves the double-transfer: the call gesture was provisional and Elijah retained ('had entire') the mantle, which only fell to Elisha at the ascension — naming both verses.

excerpts.excerpt_text: he loved this cloak ever since it was first cast over him, Kg1 19:19. He that then so cheerfully obeyed the summons of it, and became Elihah's servant, is now dignified with it, and becomes his successor.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Treats the first casting (1 Kgs 19:19) and the post-ascension receipt (2 Kgs 2:13) as one continuous calling — first the summons, now the succession — not two competing transfers.

pd_work.resource: Matthew Henry, Commentary on the Whole Bible (1706-14), on 1 Kings 19:19
pd_work.author: Matthew Henry
pd_work.note: Henry treats this passage directly, explaining that Elijah only cast the mantle on Elisha as a sign at the call but 'had the mantle entire' at his ascension (2 Kgs 2:13), so there is one transfer, not two competing ones.

link.note: No allowlisted page (gotquestions.org / carm.org / defendinginerrancy.com) squarely engages the two-transfer timing tension citing both 1 Kings 19:19 and 2 Kings 2:13; gotquestions Elijah-and-Elisha.html and life-Elisha.html describe each event but do not treat the apparent contradiction, so the optional link is omitted rather than guessed.
